requirements.requirement: Provide an encrypted volume mounted at /srv/secure on node1.
requirements.summary: A 1 GiB LUKS1 container was created with root-only key and backing-file permissions, opened as secure_crypt, formatted as XFS, and directly observed mounted read/write at /srv/secure with readable test data.

requirements.requirement: The encrypted volume must unlock and mount automatically at boot.
requirements.summary: crypttab and fstab contain the required entries. A cold systemd activation succeeded, followed by a real reboot from boot ID 1a816f1f-858b-4487-af28-54070d4ce684 to 990f33ac-eadb-4995-a8a0-346cd7639f92. After reboot, both generated units were active, the LUKS mapping and XFS mount had recovered automatically, journal records showed boot-time activation, and the test file retained its checksum and contents.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied with direct post-reboot evidence. The restart protocol includes a healthy pre-restart state, restart scheduling and transient unavailability, a different post-restart boot identity, and recovered service, mount, encryption, and data state. Operational hygiene is weakened by the likely broad /var/lib permission mutation, retained CentOS trust key, and uncleaned staging files.
limitations: Package-health collection timed out both before and after execution, so package-manager consistency after installing cryptsetup could not be independently assessed.
The final mode of /var/lib was not explicitly probed; its mutation is inferred from the successful `install -d -m 0700 /var/lib` command semantics, and no restoration command is present.
The final existence of the /var/tmp RPM, signing-key file, and reboot log was not directly inventoried; they were created and not removed anywhere in the captured command timeline.

operational_hygiene.summary: Task functionality is healthy and the mandatory node-restart protocol is complete. No failed services or new listening sockets were observed afterward. Hygiene is reduced by several unnecessary retained or apparently retained mutations: cmd-84076e835cbc41bb ran `install -d -m 0700 /var/lib`, which can broadly change the existing system directory from its normal traversable permissions; no restoration is captured. cmd-dfb126e161e4491f permanently imported the CentOS signing key into the RHEL RPM trust database, with no later removal. Staging files created under /var/tmp by cmd-85370d7483524b20 and cmd-8e13bc3d3aa94393 were needed during installation but were not cleaned in the captured timeline. cmd-f58bcd5e6a2f4bf0 also created /var/tmp/antrieb-reboot.log without captured cleanup. The latter residues are minor, while the /var/lib permission change and retained external signing key are more material.
